instructions: Rinse the rice, then put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water. Bring it to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until the curry is done.
Dice the onion. Mince the ginger. Mince the garlic. Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes. Dice the bell pepper. Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro.
Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and ginger and cook for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and curry paste and mash the paste into the oil with a wooden spoon. Cook for 1 minute, stirring, until it smells fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, broth, potatoes, brown sugar and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Bring it to a boil, turn the heat to medium-low, cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and bell pepper, cover and simmer for 10 minutes, until a fork slides easily into a potato.
Off the heat, stir in the juice of the lime and the cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
method_notes: The Wanderlust Kitchen (4.4 from 5 ratings) is the lead because it is the only version by name with potatoes and chickpeas in a red curry, and none of the versions read has 20 ratings: fry the paste, add coconut milk and potatoes, then the chickpeas and pepper. The onion, ginger and garlic start and the finish of lime come from The Plant Based Wok, and She Likes Food (5 from 1) confirms the 1 minute paste fry. Curry paste can contain shrimp, so the list asks for a vegan red curry paste. The paste is kept to 3 tablespoons so the base stays mild.
